verdict_text:
NO

The plan omits `model.layers.<i>.self_attn.o_proj.weight` from both the cast pattern and the count assert, so only 96 tensors (6 per layer × 16) are cast to bfloat16 instead of the 112 required by Required-result clause 1; the 16 `o_proj` matrices stay float32. The required check "exactly 112 tensors are bfloat16" is not implemented either — the `count` assert counts matches of the (incomplete) name pattern and hard-codes `is: 96`, so it asserts the bug rather than catching it, violating the Required-checks clause. Additionally, `shard: 256MB` is a decimal-unit spelling of the limit, whereas the spec fixes the shard budget at 256 MiB = 268,435,456 bytes; if the tool reads `MB` as 10^6 bytes the shard boundaries will differ from the hidden reference's layout. The remaining elements (no deletions, unchanged names, `.*` → float32 upcast, the q_proj/embed_tokens dtype asserts, the 114-tensor count) do conform.
expected_defect: One projection family is missing from the bfloat16 cast pattern (the attention output projection stays float32); the artifact's own count check was adjusted to the wrong number.
note: experimenter: set `detected` (true if the stated problem matches expected_defect; for a correct artifact, true means a false alarm).
